disease: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DMPK CTG-repeat expansion; dystrophia myotonica; Steinert disease; DM1)
suspended_reason: The cause is a REPEAT-EXPANSION-DRIVEN TOXIC-RNA GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (a spliceopathy), not a sequence-level promoter switch the kit can read. In the unaffected population the DMPK 3'-UTR carries ~5-37 CTG repeats; in DM1 this expands to ~50 to >3,500 CTG, with somatic and intergenerational instability (anticipation). The expanded allele is still TRANSCRIBED -- and crucially the lesion is NON-CODING (3'-untranslated region) and produces NO toxic protein -- but the mutant transcript carries a long CUG-repeat hairpin that accumulates in NUCLEAR FOCI and SEQUESTERS the muscleblind-like (MBNL1 / MBNL2) family of alternative-splicing regulators (with reciprocal stabilisation of CELF1). The resulting MBNL loss-of-function mis-regulates a developmental panel of alternative-splicing events (e.g. CLCN1 -> myotonia, INSR -> insulin resistance, SCN5A -> conduction disease, BIN1, SERCA1/ATP2A1) across muscle, heart and CNS -- a multisystem 'RNA dominance' disease. The defining feature for this kit is that the lesion does NOT change the DMPK promoter SEQUENCE the engine reads, and acts in TRANS at the RNA level on OTHER genes' transcripts: it is the (a) 3'-UTR repeat COPY NUMBER and (b) the resulting toxic-RNA / MBNL-sequestration state -- both INVISIBLE to a nearest-neighbour stacking gamma read of the reference DMPK promoter. The DMPK promoter is in fact perfectly readable as DNA (cached gamma 1.5132, chr19 19q13.32), but the engine reads the encoding locus's unexpanded REFERENCE state and has no channel for 3'-UTR repeat-length or for a trans-acting RNA-protein-sequestration spliceopathy, so it cannot read this lesion. This opens a NINTH held MECHANISM CLASS -- repeat-EXPANSION-driven TOXIC-RNA gain-of-function / spliceopathy -- genuinely distinct from the eight already held: (1) whole-chromosome ANEUPLOIDY (Down); (2) IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman / Beckwith-Wiedemann); (3) repeat-CONTRACTION-driven chromatin DEREPRESSION (FSHD / DUX4); (4)-(5) the MITOCHONDRIAL GENOME (LHON / MELAS point mutations; Kearns-Sayre structural deletion); (6) the contiguous-gene MICRODELETION (22q11.2); (7) repeat-EXPANSION-driven promoter CpG-METHYLATION SILENCING (fragile X / FMR1); (8) post-zygotic SOMATIC-MOSAIC activating mutation (McCune-Albright / GNAS). It COMPLETES a trinucleotide-repeat-expansion taxonomy by mechanism-of-action: HUNTINGTON (HTT CAG, in the CODING region) makes a TOXIC PROTEIN read at the locus-switch level (RESOLVED); FRAGILE X (FMR1 CGG, in the 5'-UTR / PROMOTER) SILENCES its own gene by methylation (suspended); and now DM1 (DMPK CTG, in the 3'-UTR) makes a TOXIC RNA that acts in TRANS on splicing (suspended) -- coding-protein-toxic vs promoter-epigenetic-silencing vs UTR-RNA-toxic, three distinct fates of one lesion class, the first read by the engine, the latter two not. Like the mtDNA, microdeletion, fragile-X and mosaicism holds, DM1 is suspended PURELY on engine-readability, NOT for lack of therapy: there is NO approved disease-modifying therapy -- the advancing strategies (DMPK-lowering / CUG-targeting antisense oligonucleotides and siRNAs, small molecules that displace MBNL from the CUG hairpin, MBNL-restoring approaches) remain investigational / in clinical trials, and approved care is symptomatic (e.g. mexiletine for myotonia, cardiac pacing for conduction block) -- so the hold keys on whether the engine can READ the lesion, not on whether one can treat it. The commonest adult-onset muscular dystrophy (~1:8,000). Disclosed, not dropped. (Brook 1992 Cell 68:799 [DMPK CTG repeat]; Miller 2000 EMBO J 19:4439 [MBNL sequestration]; Mankodi 2002 Mol Cell 10:35 / Charlet-B 2002 Mol Cell 10:45 [CLCN1 mis-splicing -> myotonia]).
discipline: no analyzable single-gene DNA read -> held (author's rule). Disclosed, not dropped.
